name: FeatureRequest
description: Public feature request and feedback API for projects and issues.

notes: The portable Agent Plugins MCP configuration leaves authorization client-managed, as required by Agent Plugins 1.0.0.
The Codex-native MCP configuration reads FEATURE_REQUEST_API_TOKEN for local authenticated development.
Both checked-in MCP URLs target the local development server.
A production plugin release must use the deployed public HTTPS MCP URL.

prompt_presets.name: portfolio-triage
prompt_presets.description: Read-only queue snapshot across all projects owned by the authenticated user.

prompt_presets.name: project-triage
prompt_presets.description: Read-only queue snapshot for one owner_handle/project_slug.

prompt_presets.name: project-implementation
prompt_presets.description: Use one project's FeatureRequest issues as the source of truth for local repo implementation work.

scope_rules: If a project_slug is provided, read only that owner_handle/project_slug unless the user explicitly expands scope.
Use provided raw API tokens directly as Bearer tokens; agent-token connect/refresh endpoints are only for web-session onboarding.
Treat queue signals, similarity scores, and delivery links as evidence; the calling agent owns priority, duplicate, and delivery-verification judgments.
Before project deletion, read the project by id and proceed only with explicit user direction.
Do not mark issues done automatically after code changes; reserve done/closed for merge or release confirmation.
recommended_codex_automation: Use one read-only portfolio triage automation for cross-project reporting.
Use project-scoped implementation automations only for active repos, with owner_handle and project_slug pinned in the prompt.
Pick at most one ready issue per implementation run unless instructed otherwise.

skills.name: user-request-manager
skills.description: API-only request lifecycle management for intake, prioritization, queue tracking, follow-up, and closure.
skills.trigger: Use when an agent must see and manage incoming user requests rather than implement product/code changes.
guardrails: Operate only through exposed request APIs.
Do not perform code or configuration edits.
Return blocking note when auth scope is insufficient.

notes: Prefer author_display_name for public display while preserving author_id and author_handle for backward compatibility.
duplicate_of_id is a reversible canonical-request link and never changes status or priority automatically.
delivery_artifacts_count and last_activity_at are deterministic signals, not delivery or priority decisions.

browser_only_routes.description: Widget-only intake endpoint. Requires a browser Turnstile token and email verification; agents must continue to use the authenticated create_issue endpoint.

notes: Token is created as `fr_<secret>`; only token_prefix is returned in list responses.
Read-only tokens (`can_write=false`) are rejected with 403 on write methods.
Use HTTPS in production.
Primarily used by web authentication routes and normal browser sessions.
CSRF still applies for state-changing endpoints.
MCP does not define a separate detailed scope model in P1.
The authenticated MCP client acts as the API token user.
Read-only tokens remain unable to call write API operations.
No get_connection_context tool is exposed; use list_projects when owner/project context is unknown.
MCP returns evidence and controlled mutations; the calling agent makes semantic priority, duplicate, and delivery decisions.

tools.name: delete_project
tools.guardrail: Call get_project first, require explicit user direction, and pass a matching confirm_project_id.

tools.name: get_queue_snapshot
tools.semantics: Returns current fields and deterministic signals; does not recommend priority.

tools.name: find_duplicate_candidates
tools.semantics: Returns a versioned lexical similarity algorithm, components, and matched terms; does not classify duplicates.

tools.name: link_duplicate_request
tools.semantics: Reversible; does not change status or priority.

tools.name: link_delivery_artifact
tools.semantics: Stores an evidence URL; does not verify delivery.

tools.name: transition_request
tools.guardrail: Do not use done or closed without explicit user direction and merge or release evidence.

rate_limiting.note: No global request-rate limit middleware is configured. Embed verification emails are limited to three per project/email fingerprint per hour.

dependency_risks: OpenAI key required for some moderation flows; moderation failures can return 503.
Turnstile site and secret keys are required for browser embed submissions; Siteverify failures return 503.
Stripe is optional until billing routes are used.
